chapter: Complaints to Senator Eastland, FCC and WDSU
title: The FCC's reply and La Rocca's reaction
summary: The FCC replies that it has no censorship power; La Rocca says he hoped for equal time and that he then wrote WDSU for the script.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Read their answer to me what I could do.

This is a letter from the Federal Communications Commission, Washington 25, D.C. November the 23rd, 1956. Address all communications to Secretary and reply referred to 8-423-11-00-505. Mr. G. James Nick LaRocca, 2218 Constant Street, New Orleans 13, Louisiana. Dear Sir, this will acknowledge receipt of your letter of November 15, 1956 with enclosures, in which you allege that state WDSU New Orleans, Louisiana, in the course of a program broadcast of its facilities, quote, made many untrue statements, unquote, concerning you and your request, some commission, quote, action on this matter, unquote. Neither the communications acts of 1934, as amended, nor the commission's rules and regulations contain any provision which pertain to the subject matter of your complaint. In fact, Section 326 of the Act specifically prohibited the commission from exercising, quote, quote, the power of censorship over the radio communications or signals transmitted by any radio station, comma, dot, dot, dot, unquote. As you know, liability for the broadcasting of allegedly defamatory matter is governed by the applicable state law. You may therefore wish to consult private legal counsel in the matter.

The reason I wrote them, I thought they would make them give me the same time that these dirty low-down people put this program on, that I would have the same time as an American citizen to tell them my side of the story. But the Federal Radio Commission seemed different. I had to sue them. Well, now I had to try to get that script first. There's my letter to WDSU. Would you read that? All right.
